children: Ahead of quarterly results from companies like Airbnb, Booking and Expedia, travel demand data paints a mixed picture, Deutsche Bank analysts say in a note. Fewer people flew in the third quarter from a year ago, and several digital engagement datasets point to weaker trends since second quarter earnings, the analysts say. A recent survey also shows U.S. monetary concerns remain elevated, they add. On the flipside, hotels' revenue per available room trends have improved, and travelers are showing more interest than ever in alternative accommodations, among other promising signals, they say. All in, those data points "continue to point to a mixed but generally healthy travel backdrop, with higher oil prices, elevated fares and heightened monetary concerns weighing on affordability and travel intent," they say. (kelly.cloonan@wsj.com)
